title: US Equities
description: Daily prices for about 1,600 US-listed stocks from January 2025 to March 2026, rolled up from real split-adjusted one-minute bars that intraday analytics read in place, with SEC company names, CIKs and SIC codes, plus the issuers' SEC EDGAR 8-K filings, eCFR Title 17 and optional GDELT world headlines as separate document sources.
disclaimer: Real market data for a software demonstration. Not investment advice.

provenance.title: US equities one-minute bars and GDELT world headlines, with SEC company metadata
provenance.notes: The bars become the market tables; the GDELT headlines are the opt-in world_news corpus, read in place. Company names, CIKs and exchanges come from SEC's company_tickers_exchange.json, and SIC codes from each company's EDGAR submissions, fetched at prepare time with SEC_USER_AGENT and cached.

provenance.title: Electronic Code of Federal Regulations, Title 17 (versioned API snapshot)
SEC final rule, Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure (88 FR 51896), Federal Register XML
provenance.notes: The rule's summary and its appendices of amended form text: Form 8-K General Instruction B.1 and Item 1.05, Form 10-K Item 1C, Form 20-F Item 16K and Form S-3. The preamble's discussion is left out.

provenance.title: SEC EDGAR 8-K filings by this pack's issuers, 2025-01-02 to 2026-03-12
provenance.notes: Selected by corpus/select_filings.py from each issuer's EDGAR submissions: every 8-K reporting Item 1.05, plus the latest 12 8-Ks of each issuer of the 100 most liquid stocks.

sources.name: US Equities
sources.description: Daily prices for about 1,600 US-listed stocks, rolled up from real one-minute bars, with SEC company data.
sources.agent_description: Real daily prices (January 2, 2025 to March 12, 2026) of US-listed stocks, with SEC names, CIKs and SIC codes, a liquidity rank and same-SIC peers. Analyze them with market analytics and SQL. There is no ticker-linked news; filings are a separate source.
example_questions: Which of the 50 most liquid stocks led returns over the latest 20 trading sessions?
Which sessions in early 2026 were most unusual among the 50 most liquid stocks?

sources.name: SEC Filings
sources.description: 8-K current reports and EX-99 exhibits filed by the companies in the pack, January 2025 to March 2026, retrieved from Milvus with NVIDIA Nemotron Embed and Rerank.
sources.agent_description: Retrieve citation-ready 8-K filings and EX-99 exhibits by companies in market_data, filed from January 2, 2025 to March 12, 2026: every 8-K reporting Item 1.05, and the latest 8-Ks of the 100 most liquid stocks. A separate document source: each passage names its company and ticker, but filings are not joined to the price tables.
example_questions: Which companies in the pack reported a material cybersecurity incident under Item 1.05?

sources.name: Market Regulations
sources.description: Current public eCFR Title 17 sections and the SEC's 2023 cybersecurity disclosure rule, retrieved from Milvus with NVIDIA Nemotron Embed and Rerank.
sources.agent_description: Retrieve citation-ready sections from the reviewed eCFR Title 17 snapshot for securities and commodities regulation research, and the form text the SEC's 2023 cybersecurity disclosure rule adopted (Form 8-K Item 1.05 and its filing deadline, Form 10-K Item 1C), which the CFR does not hold.
example_questions: What current SEC disclosure requirements apply to a material cybersecurity incident?

sources.name: World Headlines
sources.description: 8,192 GDELT world news headlines from January 2025 to February 2026 (opt-in), retrieved from Milvus with NVIDIA Nemotron Embed and Rerank.
sources.agent_description: Retrieve short world news headlines sampled from GDELT, with their outlet and date. They are not linked to any stock or filing, and many are topic summaries rather than article titles.
example_questions: Which headlines mention the Federal Reserve?

questions.label: Market Leaders
questions.description: Scan the 50 most liquid US stocks for their strongest and weakest recent returns.
questions.question: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which had the strongest and weakest returns over the 20 trading sessions ending March 12, 2026, and how did their daily volatility compare?

questions.label: Intraday Swings
questions.description: Scan real one-minute bars for the sessions with the widest intraday swings.
questions.question: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which sessions from March 2 through March 12, 2026 had the widest intraday price ranges? For each, how did it trade from open to close, and how much of its volume came in the last 30 minutes?

questions.label: Unusual Sessions
questions.description: Rank unusual return, volatility and volume combinations across the 50 most liquid stocks.
questions.question: Using 2025 as the baseline, which 10 sessions from January 2 through March 12, 2026 were the most unusual among the 50 most liquid US stocks, and which features made each one unusual? Anomaly scores are neither forecasts nor explanations.

questions.label: Peer Network
questions.description: Find the most central stocks in the return-correlation network of same-industry peers.
questions.question: Among declared industry peers, which stocks were the most central in the return-correlation network from December 2025 through March 12, 2026, and which pairs moved together most closely?

questions.label: Cybersecurity Disclosures
questions.description: Pair the Form 8-K Item 1.05 rule with filings by companies in the pack that report an incident.
questions.question: What does Form 8-K Item 1.05 require a company to disclose about a material cybersecurity incident, and by when? Cite the regulation, and any 8-K filings in the corpus that report an incident under Item 1.05.

questions.label: Moves & Filings
questions.description: Price moves and SEC filings as two separate sources, joined only by company.
questions.question: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which three had the strongest and which three the weakest returns in February 2026? Separately, what did those six companies disclose in their 8-K filings from January through March 2026? Report the moves and the filings apart, and do not claim that a filing caused a move.

questions.label: Whole-Market Scan
questions.description: Scan the 500 most liquid stocks at once.
questions.question: Across the 500 most liquid US stocks, which 20 had the strongest and the weakest returns from January 2 to March 12, 2026, and how unusual was their trading volume?

questions.label: Five-Session Outlook
questions.description: Rank the 50 most liquid stocks with a five-session prediction anchored before the outcomes.
questions.question: As of the March 5, 2026 market close, which of the 50 most liquid stocks are most likely to post a positive five-session return?

questions.label: Sector Breakdown
questions.description: Count stocks and summarize returns by SIC division with SQL.
questions.question: How many stocks are in each SIC division, and what was each division's median return from January 2 to March 12, 2026?

questions.label: World Headlines
questions.description: Search the optional GDELT world news headlines, a source that is not linked to any stock.
questions.question: Which world news headlines in the corpus mention the Federal Reserve or another central bank? List their outlets and dates, and cite the headlines.

questions.label: Volatility Ranking
questions.description: Rank the 50 most liquid stocks by daily volatility over 60 sessions, with their returns.
questions.question: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which five had the highest and which five the lowest daily volatility over the 60 trading sessions ending March 12, 2026, and what were their returns over those sessions?

questions.label: Peer-Relative Returns
questions.description: Find the stocks that beat or trailed the group's average return by the most.
questions.question: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which five beat the group's average return by the most, and which five trailed it by the most, over the 20 trading sessions ending March 12, 2026?

questions.label: Second Half of 2025
questions.description: Scan the 500 most liquid stocks for the strongest and weakest returns of the second half of 2025.
questions.question: Among the 500 most liquid US stocks, which 10 had the strongest and which 10 the weakest returns from July 1 through December 31, 2025, and how volatile was each one's daily trading?

questions.label: Intraday Drawdowns
questions.description: Scan real one-minute bars for the deepest falls from a session's running high.
questions.question: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which 10 sessions from February 2 through February 27, 2026 had the deepest drawdowns from the session's running high, and how did each one close relative to its open?

questions.label: Heaviest Sessions
questions.description: Rank the sessions with the most shares traded, and show when in the day the volume came.
questions.question: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which 10 sessions from March 9 through March 12, 2026 traded the most shares, and how much of each session's volume came in its first and last 30 minutes?

questions.label: April 2025 Anomalies
questions.description: Score April 2025's sessions against a PCA model of the first quarter.
questions.question: Using January 2 through March 31, 2025 as the baseline, which 10 sessions in April 2025 were the most unusual among the 50 most liquid US stocks, and which features made each one unusual? Anomaly scores are neither forecasts nor explanations.

questions.label: Q4 2025 Anomalies
questions.description: Score the fourth quarter of 2025 against the three before it, across the 500 most liquid stocks.
questions.question: Using January 2 through September 30, 2025 as the baseline, which 15 sessions in the fourth quarter of 2025 were the most unusual among the 500 most liquid US stocks, and which features made each one unusual? Anomaly scores are neither forecasts nor explanations.

questions.label: Central Industries
questions.description: Name the industries of the most central stocks in the peer return-correlation network.
questions.question: Which 10 stocks were the most central in the declared-peer return-correlation network from December 2025 through March 12, 2026, and which SEC industries are they in?

questions.label: Downside Outlook
questions.description: Rank the 50 most liquid stocks by the predicted chance of a five-session fall of more than 5%.
questions.question: As of the March 5, 2026 market close, which of the 50 most liquid US stocks are most likely to fall more than 5% over the next five sessions?

questions.label: Named-Stock Outlook
questions.description: Predict both five-session outcomes for five named stocks.
questions.question: As of the March 5, 2026 market close, how likely are NVIDIA (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Tesla (TSLA) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) to post a positive five-session return, and how likely is each to fall more than 5%?

questions.label: Exchange Listings
questions.description: Count the pack's stocks by listing exchange with SQL.
questions.question: How many stocks in the pack are listed on each exchange, and how many of the 500 and of the 50 most liquid are on each?

questions.label: Big-Move Days
questions.description: Count each liquid stock's 2025 sessions with a daily move of more than 10%.
questions.question: Among the 500 most liquid US stocks, which 10 had the most sessions in 2025 with a close-to-close move of more than 10% in either direction, and what were their largest rise and fall?

questions.label: Executive Changes
questions.description: Summarize 8-K filings about executive and director changes (Item 5.02).
questions.question: Which companies filed 8-Ks under Item 5.02 about executive or director changes in January and February 2026? Summarize three of them, and cite the filings.

questions.label: Material Agreements
questions.description: Summarize 8-K filings about entering or ending material agreements (Items 1.01 and 1.02).
questions.question: Which 8-K filings from February and March 2026 report entering into or terminating a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01 or 1.02? Summarize three of the agreements, and cite the filings.

questions.label: Restructuring Costs
questions.description: Find 8-K filings that disclose exit or restructuring costs (Item 2.05).
questions.question: Which companies disclosed exit or restructuring costs under 8-K Item 2.05, and what charges did each expect? Cite the filings.

questions.label: Beneficial Ownership
questions.description: Explain the Schedule 13D and 13G filing deadlines in Title 17.
questions.question: Under Title 17, when must a person who acquires more than five percent of a class of registered equity securities file a Schedule 13D, and when may they file a Schedule 13G instead? Cite the sections.

questions.label: Shareholder Proposals
questions.description: Explain Rule 14a-8's eligibility requirements for shareholder proposals.
questions.question: Under Rule 14a-8 in Title 17, what ownership and holding-period requirements must a shareholder meet to have a proposal included in a company's proxy statement? Cite the section.

questions.label: Cyber Headlines
questions.description: Search the optional GDELT world news headlines for cyber attacks.
questions.question: Which world news headlines in the corpus are about cyber attacks? List their outlets and dates, and cite the headlines.

questions.label: NVIDIA Prices & Filings
questions.description: NVIDIA's price context and its 8-K filings, as two separate sources.
questions.question: How did NVIDIA (NVDA) trade from February 2 through March 12, 2026? Separately, what did its 8-K filings in that period disclose? Report the prices and the filings apart, and do not claim that a filing caused a move.

questions.label: Bank Results
questions.description: Five large banks' January 2026 moves beside their results 8-Ks, kept apart.
questions.question: How did JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs trade in January 2026? Separately, what did their January 2026 results 8-Ks report? Report the moves and the filings apart, and do not claim that a filing caused a move.

conversations.label: Price Context Follow-up
conversations.description: Summarize two stocks' daily price context, then add a third and aggregate the series weekly.
turns: Summarize the daily price context for NVIDIA (NVDA) and Apple (AAPL) from February 2 through February 27, 2026, including each stock's return, price range and average volume.
Keep that same window and add Microsoft (MSFT), but aggregate the displayed series weekly.

conversations.label: Peer Network Follow-up
conversations.description: Find the most central peers, then compare their returns and volatility over the same window.
turns: Among declared industry peers, which five stocks were the most central in the return-correlation network from December 2025 through March 12, 2026?
For the three most central stocks in that result, compare their returns and daily volatility over the same window.

conversations.label: Leaders & Unusual Sessions
conversations.description: Rank the strongest and weakest recent returns, then check those stocks for unusual sessions.
turns: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which three had the strongest and which three the weakest returns over the 20 trading sessions ending March 12, 2026?

Using 2025 as the baseline, did any of those six stocks have unusual sessions in that same window? Name the sessions and the features that made each one unusual. Anomaly scores are neither forecasts nor explanations.

conversations.label: Filings & Regulations
conversations.description: Pick two 8-K cybersecurity incident filings, then compare them with the Title 17 requirements.
turns: Which 8-K filings in the corpus report a cybersecurity incident under Item 1.05? Select two examples with materially different disclosed impacts, and cite the filings.
For those same two examples, compare the disclosed facts with the Title 17 cybersecurity incident disclosure requirements, and identify what the evidence does not establish.

conversations.label: Regulation FD Follow-up
conversations.description: When Regulation FD requires public disclosure, then intentional and unintentional cases apart.
turns: Under Regulation FD in Title 17, when must an issuer publicly disclose material nonpublic information that it shared with certain persons outside the company? Cite the relevant sections.
Now separate the intentional and the unintentional selective disclosure cases, and say how the issuer may make the public disclosure, keeping the section citations.

conversations.label: Mega-Cap Follow-up
conversations.description: Summarize four large stocks' price context, then compare it with the previous quarter, monthly.
turns: Summarize the price context for Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL) from January 2 through March 12, 2026, including each stock's return, price range and average volume.
Keep the same four stocks and compare that with October 1 through December 31, 2025, aggregating both series monthly.

conversations.label: April 2025 Follow-up
conversations.description: Find the steepest early-April 2025 declines, then follow those stocks through the next week.
turns: Among the 50 most liquid US stocks, which five had the weakest returns from April 1 through April 8, 2025?
How did those five stocks trade over the following sessions, from April 9 through April 15, 2025?

conversations.label: Intraday Volatility Follow-up
conversations.description: Rank minute-level volatility for three stocks, then look inside the most volatile sessions.
turns: For NVIDIA (NVDA), Tesla (TSLA) and AMD, which 10 sessions from January 2 through March 12, 2026 had the highest minute-by-minute realized volatility?
For the three most volatile of those sessions, how did each trade from open to close, what was its VWAP, and how much of its volume came in the last 30 minutes?

conversations.label: Prediction Follow-up
conversations.description: Rank a five-session outlook, then compare it with the returns that followed.
turns: As of the March 5, 2026 market close, which five of the 50 most liquid US stocks are most likely to post a positive five-session return?
What were those five stocks' actual returns from the March 5 close through March 12, 2026? Compare them with the predictions, without treating one week as a test of the model.

conversations.label: Peer Links Follow-up
conversations.description: List the strongest peer correlations, then compare the strongest pair's returns.
turns: In the declared-peer return-correlation network from December 2025 through March 12, 2026, which 10 pairs of stocks were the most strongly correlated, and did any pair move in opposite directions?
For the most strongly correlated pair in that result, compare the two stocks' returns and daily volatility over the same window.

conversations.label: Sector Follow-up
conversations.description: Count stocks by SIC division, then break the largest division down by industry.
turns: How many of the pack's stocks are in each SIC division, and how many of each are among the 500 most liquid?
For the division with the most stocks among the 500 most liquid, which five industries hold the most of them?

conversations.label: Results Follow-up
conversations.description: Find five large companies' quarterly results 8-Ks, then pull the figures from two of them.
turns: Which of NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta filed quarterly results 8-Ks under Item 2.02 in January or February 2026? List each company and filing date, and cite the filings.
For the first two companies in that result, what revenue and earnings figures did their results releases report? Cite the exhibits.

conversations.label: Rule 10b5-1 Follow-up
conversations.description: Explain Rule 10b5-1 trading plan conditions, then contrast directors and officers with others.
turns: What conditions does Rule 10b5-1 in Title 17 place on trading plans used for the affirmative defense, including cooling-off periods? Cite the section.
Now contrast the conditions for directors and officers with those for other persons, keeping the section citations.

conversations.label: Headlines & Prices
conversations.description: World headlines that mention Nvidia, then NVDA's prices that month, as separate sources.
turns: Which world news headlines from February 2025 mention Nvidia? List their outlets and dates, and cite the headlines.
Separately, how did NVIDIA (NVDA) trade in February 2025? Report the prices apart from the headlines, and do not claim that a headline caused a move.

conversations.label: Incidents & Prices
conversations.description: Item 1.05 cybersecurity incident filings, then the filers' prices after each, kept apart.
turns: Which companies reported a material cybersecurity incident on Form 8-K under Item 1.05, and when did each file? Cite the filings.
How did each of those companies' stocks trade over the five sessions after its filing? Report the prices separately from the filings, and do not claim that a filing caused a move.

top_50.description: The 50 most liquid stocks, by median daily dollar volume through the prediction anchor.

templates.name: Positive five-session return
templates.description: Rank the 50 most liquid stocks by likelihood of a positive five-session adjusted-close return realized within 5 calendar days after the anchor.
templates.pql: PREDICT COUNT(return_outcomes.* WHERE return_outcomes.positive_return = true, 0, 5, days) > 0 FOR EACH asset_entities.asset_id

templates.name: Material five-session downside
templates.description: Rank the 50 most liquid stocks by likelihood of a five-session adjusted-close return below negative five percent realized within 5 calendar days after the anchor.
templates.pql: PREDICT COUNT(return_outcomes.* WHERE return_outcomes.forward_return_5d < -0.05, 0, 5, days) > 0 FOR EACH asset_entities.asset_id

share repurchase program authorizations and the rules for issuer repurchases
